profile.headline: Software Engineer at Ocient
profile.summary: My goal is to become a valuable asset in a challenging work environment, solving problems as a software engineer

positions.title: Machine Learning Research Assistant
positions.description:
・Assisting Dr. Brian Ziebart in development of an adversarial cost-sensitive classification framework (minimax game for multivariate loss optimization)
・Finding solutions to minimax games using the following scoring objectives:

     - mean average precision (greedy solution ends up being suboptimal)
     - ROC area curve (np-complete, "minimum weighted feedback arc"​ problem)
     - reciprocal rank (np-hard, "set coverage" problem)
     - percent error reduction (in progress)
     - precision-recall break even point (in progress)

•	Developed CMS features under Rails framework (TDD) in a very agile environment
•	Wrote SQL database queries to generate operational reports and customer analysis

projects.title: Automatic TOEFL essay grader, UIC CS 421: Natural Language Processing
projects.description:
・Developed a classifier for scoring essays on the following features: spelling, subject-verb agreement, verb tense agreement, sentence formation, pronoun reference, topic accuracy and length
・Utilized NLTK, Stanford NLP and CLiPS frameworks to assist in scoring each feature
・Weights for each feature were predetermined (not a supervised learning project)
・System placed 3rd out of 22 participating teams (based on accuracy)

projects.title: Yelp dataset challenge, UIC CS 491: Intro to Machine Learning
projects.description:
・Objective: find factors which contribute most to a restaurant’s Yelp rating using written reviews. 
・Leveraged Latent Dirichlet allocation to discover the top 3 features (location, service, price)
・Manually labeled ~10,000 reviews for feature sentiment.
・Used both supervised (SVM & Logistic Reg.) and unsupervised (Spatial Clustering) methods
